memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: Sacrifice as the Passover to the Lord your God an animal from your flock or herd at the place the Lord will choose as a dwelling for his Name. Do not eat it with bread made with yeast, but for seven days eat unleavened bread, the bread of affliction, because you left Egypt in haste—so that all the days of your life you may remember the time of your departure from Egypt. - Deut 16:2-3 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God ties the meal to a place, "the place the Lord will choose," and to a taste, the plain, flat bread of a people leaving in a hurry. There was no time to let the dough rise. This simple bread carried a whole memory in it. God called it "the bread of affliction," a reminder of the hardship they had known and the sudden freedom He gave.

Every year the taste of that bread would take them back. God knows we are forgetful creatures, so He built remembrance into their meals, their calendar, their very palate. The goal was clear, "so that all the days of your life you may remember."

There is tender wisdom here for us. God does not ask us to summon big feelings out of nowhere. He gives us simple, tangible things, bread and cup, gathered worship, His written Word, to keep His faithfulness in front of us. The unleavened bread also pointed to a life cleared of the old corruption of sin, a theme the New Testament picks up as it calls us to sincerity and truth (1 Cor 5:8). Let ordinary reminders do their work in you today.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What ordinary things help you remember God's goodness?
2. Why do you think God links memory to something as simple as bread?
3. Is there old "yeast" in your life He is asking you to clear out?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, thank You for building remembrance into simple things. Help me clear out the old sin and live in sincerity and truth. Amen.
